findings: src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp: lowering PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD from 1M to 64K rows is a general tuning change. It doesn't depend on any query, table or data. The num_threads==1 and KeysAreSkewed fallbacks still route to the serial path.

Correctness: builds over 1M rows already use the parallel path (InsertHashesLoop<true> with CAS chain insert). Both bloom filter inserts are atomic: hashed BF InsertHashes (bloom_filter.cpp:82) and exact BF InsertExact (bloom_filter.hpp:63) use fetch_or with relaxed ordering. Builds of 64K-1M rows use that same thread-safe code, so there is no new race.

The adaptive chunks_per_task = clamp(chunk_count/(4*num_threads), 4, 64) cannot divide by zero. The parallel path is only taken when num_threads >= 2, and verify_parallelism still uses 1 chunk per task. Builds over 1M rows are unchanged in practice, because chunk_count/(4*threads) is at least 64 at typical thread counts.
No extra threads are used beyond the configured scheduler. The change doesn't touch measurement code, settings defaults or tests, and there is no dead or duplicated code.
